parts:
Hi Felipe,

wintermelt$variable <- factor(wintermelt$variable, levels =
levels(wintermelt$variable)[c(5, 4, 1, 3, 2)])

ggplot(wintermelt, aes(WEEK,value/1000, linetype=variable, colour=variable))
+
geom_line(size=1) + theme_bw() +

scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1,52,3),labels=levels(winter$week)[seq(1,52,3)
],) +
opts(title="Winter") + labs(y="Number of fish X 1,000",x="WEEK") +
scale_colour_discrete(name = "Week run") + # better
scale_colour_brewer?
scale_linetype_discrete(name = "Week run")


1.- Not sure if the code produces the exact outpu you want, but you can
reorder the levels of the factor as you want (see
http://learnr.wordpress.com/2010/03/23/ggplot2-changing-the-default-order-of
-legend-labels-and-stacking-of-data/)

2.- I don't understand your point (I get only 5 lines)

3.- The name of the legend correspond to the scales for 'colour' and
'linetype'

Hope this helps,
fernando
